title: Triage review of c33's attractive-only phoretic negative: on fresh seed 3 the unequal all-attractive responses at kd 0.05 and 0.2 give round, static mixed A+B clusters with B toward the core; labkit max 3.2 and 2.6 body lengths come from the condensation and merge phase, 0 persistent splits
summary: I re-ran the Janus world (20261026T0254-c33-phoretic-janus-claim/world.py, 1400 A + 400 B by default) with labkit on fresh seed 3, t=200 (400 frames), at WORLD_P mu [[1, 0.2], [1.5, 0.3]] with kd 0.05 and kd 0.2, two of the finding's four settings. kd 0.05: clusters condense from the gas by t~50 and are round and still from t~100 to t=200 (rerun/u05_seed3/particles.png), with B (cyan) concentrated toward the centre; 20 bodies at the end, 25 merges and 2 splits (0 persistent); labkit reports 26 tracks >= 1 BL and a maximum of 3.2 BL (about 2.8 cluster diameters), which comes from the early condensation and merging period and not from a travelling composite in the images. kd 0.2: 44 smaller static clusters, max 2.6 BL, 9 splits, 0 persistent. This matches the finding: no self-propulsion with all-attractive unequal responses, and attraction pulls B into the body.

observations.F: rerun/u05_seed3/particles.png t=100-200: round static clusters, B central; FACTS max 3.2 BL from early merging, 0 persistent splits; rerun/u20_seed3: max 2.6 BL

not_checked: per-composite diameter travel and B rim/core with the author's cluster script (I used labkit's tracker and the images)
verdicts.limitation: Triage: two settings, one fresh seed, t=200 only, and motion judged from labkit's grid tracker plus images rather than the author's particle-cluster measure; labkit's max of 3.2 BL is near the gate and would need a merge-aware track to exclude a genuine mover.
